title: Shoppers will start with AI agents, so our store must be agent-ready
summary: Amazon let select US customers shop by texting Alexa; Walmart added cart generation to Sparky; OpenAI opened claimable ChatGPT business profiles; Visa found AI models fail 43% of shopping tests. Memory shortage seen lasting through 2028.

points.headline: Agent shopping is going mainstream on Amazon and Walmart, though still error-prone
points.detail: Amazon opened text-to-shop via Alexa and a merchant workspace; Walmart's Sparky builds carts; Visa found a 43% failure rate. We should make our listings and checkout agent-readable and test them.

points.headline: AI platforms are opening business profiles while the EU moves to regulate agents
points.detail: OpenAI lets businesses claim ChatGPT profiles and adds agents for US e-commerce firms; an EU draft law ties shopping agents’ autonomy to commercial incentives. We should claim profiles and track the rules.

points.headline: Payment and financing rails are being rebuilt for AI agents
points.detail: Cashfree launched Checkout for Agents and Affirm's CEO expects agents to favor interest-free instalments. We should make sure our financing offers and checkout can be used by agent-initiated purchases.

points.headline: Memory shortage and soft laptop demand squeeze PC pricing
points.detail: Samsung sees the memory shortage lasting through 2028 and Simplo reports softer peak-season laptop demand, while Apple plans 16M MacBook Neo units in 2027. We should plan pricing and promotions cautiously.

points.headline: Amazon fees rise and TikTok Shop deepens loyalty, shifting channel economics
points.detail: Amazon seller fees and ads reached $66.1B in Q3; TikTok Shop launched a paid Plus membership for top US shoppers. We should weigh marketplace margin against growing our own store.
